path: Existing owned pipeline source -> original issued actor and canonical repository owner -> current GitHub connection -> fixed bounded release metadata -> inspected private source manifest in existing project_files/DB or private R2 -> existing business_action_confirmations -> explicit current-user confirmation -> canonical durable claim and permit -> producer attestation, current owner/source epoch/credential/target -> central egress decision and immutable audit -> exact one-time release creation/asset replacement/upload sequence -> verified uploaded asset receipt and canonical consumed/failure receipt.
defectsFixed: Both native helpers uploaded source without durable consequential approval.
No immutable approved source, project ownership, credential metadata, release ID or replacement asset binding survived a confirmation wait.
Pipeline could claim publication or start another native operation without the new exact approval.
controls: Original WeakSet-issued context, exact owner and repository lookup. No raw-ID or fabricated permit fallback.

Preparation performs no GitHub mutation. Source is inspected before compression and stored through existing owner-private storage, with digest, file identity, delivery epoch and deterministic ZIP digest. No new store, key, schema or orchestrator.

Existing managed vault producer attestation binds the complete unsigned plan, including owner, tenant, project, account, arguments, expiry, nonce and risk. A request or changed JSONB row cannot mint a plan.

Current full canonical GitHub row and token are pinned. Exact private source and owned file epoch are re-read before effect admission. Revocation, cancellation, rotation and changed target are terminal.

The existing canonical confirmation executor claims once. Central egress persists a safe decision before consuming its genuine permit. Subsequent planned subeffects require the same current executing durable record and exact sequence. No denied/uncertain retry or store/Actions fallback.

Only fixed GitHub metadata and exact release asset destinations are allowed. Redirect/auth denial cannot become release creation or upload. Replacement requires the approved old asset and DELETE204. Publication requires the exact uploaded asset ID/name/size/state/download URL.
Native source path aliases, credential files, held platform/provider secrets and their common encodings are rejected before ZIP serialization. Generic binary egress policy remains unchanged.

Existing UI confirmation shows exact repository/tag/artifact identity and replacement intent. Actual pipeline tests execute its original block and require the approval link, no fake success and no installer/store action while publication is pending.

Provider HTTP operations in this adapter do not purchase a model/build service. Canonical durable effect receipts account for the exact publication. Separate paid Actions/build admission remains an unresolved shared-caller obligation.

tests.scope: Actual helpers and canonical business-action confirmation/claim/dispatch/finish code through real Supabase SDK HTTP contracts against synthetic fixtures, actual pipeline native block execution, existing signing routes and signing admission tests, and unchanged business-action digest, claim, preview and risk tests. No real GitHub publication or customer-data access.

limitations: Shared ghFetch/Actions, Chrome Web Store, Expo, provisioning, Composio and Parallel remain pending independently. No upstream caller is promoted by these two upload closures.

Small source-manifest storage/readback executes against synthetic database fixtures. The unchanged larger-file R2 adapter retains its existing independent evidence, not a newly claimed live R2 upload.
No merge, deployment, production mutation, live provider call or cloud spending. Exact-source CI and final current-main release integration are still required.
